name: Kyndryl Holdings, Inc.
business: Kyndryl runs, modernizes and secures mission-critical IT infrastructure (cloud, mainframe, network, security) for large enterprises, mostly banks, retailers and industrials, worldwide.

events.what: CFO David Wyshner and General Counsel Edward Sebold departed; Global Controller moved to another role; interim CFO (Harsh Chugh) and interim Controller appointed. Material weaknesses later disclosed: senior finance executives 'failed to set an appropriate tone at the top', including disclosure around 'cash management practices regarding deferring vendor payments quarter to quarter'
events.from: Chugh: Kyndryl COO 2021 to January 2026, ex IBM
Former EVP and CFO of Interpublic Group
events.source: 8-K 0001104659-26-080558 (appointment, filed 2026-07-06); doc 112264 (AGM 2026, Schroeter: 'will assume the CFO on August 6th')

events.what: Workforce rebalancing program: about $200M of charges in fiscal 2027, annualized savings of $400M to $500M in fiscal 2028

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework update announced in Baba. The fiscal Q2 2027 call (date not announced) will be Ellen Johnson's first as CFO. Material weakness remediation is targeted for 2027-03-31 (doc 112264, Schroeter, AGM 2026-07-30). The last Investor Day was 2024-11-21 (doc 68122).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: The EBITDA margin target (20% to 22% in fiscal 2028, set by former CFO Wyshner at the 2024-11-21 Investor Day on $16B to $17B of revenue) has not been repeated in any 2026 call in Baba. The repeated targets are adjusted pretax income above $1.2B and free cash flow of $1B in fiscal 2028 (CEO Schroeter, most recently 2026-08-05, now on 'low single-digit' revenue growth). $1.2B on FY2028 consensus revenue of $14.84B is about an 8.1% pretax margin ('high single digits'). The gap below uses the EBITDA target because consensus pretax income is not in Baba. EBITDA is a weak metric here: EV/EBITDA of 1.6x reflects heavy capitalized-cost amortization, so pretax income and FCF are what the market prices. Fiscal year ends March; Baba FY2028 = company fiscal 2028 (ending Mar-2028).

statements.quote: As our adjusted pre-tax margins move up to the high single digits, we will have a similar uptick in our adjusted EBITDA margin, which we see increasing 370-570 basis points to 20%-22% in fiscal 2028.
statements.speaker: David Wyshner

statements.quote: the quality of that revenue base gives us confidence in our ability to increase profitability and deliver more than $1.2 billion in adjusted pre-tax income and $1 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2028. These targets can be achieved on low single-digit constant currency revenue growth.
statements.speaker: Martin Schroeter
statements.doc_title: Kyndryl Holdings Inc Q1 2027 Earnings Call

statements.quote: This pre-tax income outlook includes approximately $200 million of workforce rebalancing charges and a similar amount of savings associated with these actions to offset the charges. In fiscal 2028, these actions are expected to yield annualized savings in the range of $400 million-$500 million.
statements.speaker: Harsh Chugh
statements.doc_title: Kyndryl Holdings Inc Q1 2027 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: Target midpoint 21% adjusted EBITDA margin in fiscal 2028 versus VA FY2028 (FYE Mar-2028) consensus of 19.02%; +98 bps against the 20% low end. FY2026 is reported (fiscal year ended Mar-2026). The target assumed $16B to $17B of revenue; consensus FY2028 revenue is $14.84B, and management now cites only the pretax income and FCF targets.

evidence_of_progress.note: VA EBITDA margin yoy: fiscal Q3 2026 -79 bps, fiscal Q4 2026 -11 bps, after +240 and +250 bps in Q1 and Q2 (Wyshner, docs 51829 and 51827). Fiscal 2026 adjusted pretax income was $581M (Chugh, doc 188392) against an initial guide of at least $725M (Wyshner, doc 51831). Fiscal Q1 2027 adjusted EBITDA was $512M (vs $647M a year earlier) with a $37M adjusted pretax loss, including $152M of workforce charges (doc 129669); VA has not loaded Q1 FY2027 actuals. FY2027 guide: pretax income $600M to $700M, FCF $400M to $500M, revenue flat to down 2% in constant currency.

verdict: Scores 9 on the rubric, but the catalyst is a forced finance clean-up after material weaknesses tied to deferring vendor payments; margins slipped and the targets now rest on cost cuts.
open_questions: Does Ellen Johnson keep the fiscal 2028 targets ($1.2B+ pretax income, $1B FCF) on her first call, or re-base them, and what happened to the 20% to 22% EBITDA margin target?
How much of past free cash flow came from deferring vendor payments, and what is the normalized FCF once those are unwound?
Are the $400M to $500M of fiscal 2028 workforce savings in consensus, given FY2028 EBITDA consensus is only $145M above FY2027?
